scenarioStory.history: 70-year-old male found by his daughter slumped in his recliner, unusually drowsy and slow to respond. She states he has seemed "off" and weak since this afternoon. An empty bottle of metoprolol tartrate 100 mg, refilled 3 days ago, was found on the side table with far fewer pills remaining than expected. Patient is arousable to voice, denies chest pain, admits to feeling "foggy" and lightheaded. No witnessed seizure, no vomiting.
scenarioStory.course: Initial Contact: Crew arrives to find a 70-year-old male slumped in his recliner, pale and diaphoretic, slow to arouse. Radial pulses are slow and weak. Family reports an empty metoprolol bottle and possible overdose. → Atropine Given: Crew manages airway, applies oxygen and the cardiac monitor, obtains a 12-lead EKG, establishes IV access, checks blood glucose, and administers atropine per the Bradycardia and Beta Blocker Overdose guidelines. HR and BP show minimal improvement. → Glucagon Given: Atropine has little effect, consistent with beta-blocker toxicity. Crew administers glucagon and a fluid bolus for hypotension. HR and BP improve modestly but the patient remains symptomatic. → TCP Initiated: Bradycardia and hypotension are refractory to atropine, glucagon, and fluids. Crew provides sedation and initiates transcutaneous pacing, achieving electrical and mechanical capture, with improvement in heart rate and blood pressure.

patientInformation.patientCondition: Weakness and dizziness; family found him slow to respond with a slow pulse

scenarioEvents.name: Initial Contact
scenarioEvents.description: Crew arrives to find a 70-year-old male slumped in his recliner, pale and diaphoretic, slow to arouse. Radial pulses are slow and weak. Family reports an empty metoprolol bottle and possible overdose.
relatedChecklist: Recognize symptomatic bradycardia (HR 38 with hypotension and AMS)
Obtain ingestion history: medication, time, quantity from daughter and pill bottle
Collect pill bottle and bring to ED with patient

scenarioEvents.name: Atropine Given
scenarioEvents.description: Crew manages airway, applies oxygen and the cardiac monitor, obtains a 12-lead EKG, establishes IV access, checks blood glucose, and administers atropine per the Bradycardia and Beta Blocker Overdose guidelines. HR and BP show minimal improvement.
relatedChecklist: Initiate cardiac monitor and obtain 12-lead EKG
Check blood glucose (beta-blockers can cause hypoglycemia)
Atropine 1 mg IV push (fixed adult dose; may repeat q5min to max 3 mg)

scenarioEvents.name: Glucagon Given
scenarioEvents.description: Atropine has little effect, consistent with beta-blocker toxicity. Crew administers glucagon and a fluid bolus for hypotension. HR and BP improve modestly but the patient remains symptomatic.
relatedChecklist: Glucagon 5 mg IVP (fixed adult dose; may repeat in 5-10 min, max 10 mg total)
Normal saline bolus 1,680 mL IV (84 kg x 20 mL/kg) for hypotension
Defer activated charcoal - ingestion occurred approximately 2 hours prior, outside 1-hour window

scenarioEvents.name: TCP Initiated
scenarioEvents.description: Bradycardia and hypotension are refractory to atropine, glucagon, and fluids. Crew provides sedation and initiates transcutaneous pacing, achieving electrical and mechanical capture, with improvement in heart rate and blood pressure.
relatedChecklist: Administer sedation/analgesia prior to transcutaneous pacing
Initiate transcutaneous pacing at 70 bpm; titrate mA until electrical and mechanical capture confirmed
Consider norepinephrine infusion 1.7-33.6 mcg/min IV (84 kg x 0.02-0.4 mcg/kg/min) titrated to MAP >65 mmHg if hypotension persists after pacing
Reassess capture, pulse quality, and blood pressure response to pacing

scenarioEvents.name: TCP Delayed
scenarioEvents.description: Crew continues to re-dose atropine rather than escalating to glucagon and transcutaneous pacing. The patient's heart rate and blood pressure continue to fall and mental status deteriorates toward unresponsiveness.
relatedChecklist: Recognize refractory bradycardia; escalate immediately to glucagon and transcutaneous pacing
